title: Two identical Curve RLUSD/USDC instance documents exist, sharing one pool address and one swap RateLimitID
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.6.1 and A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.6.2 are both titled "Ethereum Mainnet - Curve RLUSD/USDC Pool Instance Configuration Document". Every field matches: pool address `0xD001aE433f254283FeCE51d4ACcE8c53263aa186`, the same two underlying assets, RRC status `Pending`, swap limits of 20 million with a 100 million per day slope and 0.1% max slippage, and — decisively — the **same** swap RateLimitID `0x8dcb7a359e6824ce9fd1c1f50ba67cd468764f690da2589aa3c262ac142c333a`.

The shared key is what settles the interpretation. Two genuinely separate instances would necessarily have separate keys, because a key *is* the budget; sharing one means both documents describe the same on-chain state. This is duplication, not a pair.

It matters for how the Artifact is read. The Active Instances list is the register a reviewer uses to enumerate where Grove's capital can go and to sum its exposure. A duplicated entry inflates the apparent count of venues and, if the limits were naively added up, would double-count available swap capacity that in reality is one 20 million bucket.

It is also the third documentation defect in this part of the Artifact, after the duplicated-and-drifted Ethena procedures and the copy-pasted PT token addresses. The pattern suggests the instance register is maintained by hand without a uniqueness check on pool address or RateLimitID — and both of those fields would make an easy automated one.
description: A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.6.1 and .6.2 have the same title, pool, underlying assets, swap key and parameters — so they are one budget documented twice, not two instances.
